coordinates.note: The collaboration papers place GRANDProto300 qualitatively (ICRC 2025: XiaoDuShan site in Dunhuang, a 2.5-hour drive from the city; JINST, arXiv:2509.21306: the 300-antenna stage will span about 200 km² in the Gobi Desert near Xiaodushan, in northern Dunhuang, China) but give no numeric coordinates. This point is Dunhuang city itself (Wikipedia infobox, rank 12: 40°08′28″N 94°39′50″E = 40.14111, 94.66389), used only as the nearest real, named reference point; the 65-antenna array (GP300_s65, about 30 km² per the JINST paper) lies somewhere in the Gobi Desert north of the city, not at this exact point. kind is campus with confidence uncertain, per A23, because this is a city-level regional pointer, not a surveyed array position.

summary.plain: A stretch of the Gobi Desert north of the city of Dunhuang, China, where a prototype array of radio antennas is testing technology for the giant GRAND project.
summary.technical: Gobi Desert site near Xiaodushan, north of Dunhuang, Gansu, China, hosting the GRANDProto300 prototype radio array; coordinates recorded as the nearest named city (Dunhuang) as a coarse regional pointer, not a surveyed array position.
